question: Which of these should you NOT do when teaching a community during an outbreak?

options.A: Using complex medical jargon to show professional superiority
options.B: Listening carefully to community fears and answering questions
options.C: Explaining simple preventive habits like handwashing clearly
options.D: Collaborating directly with respected local and religious leaders

explanation: Never use heavy grammar or jargon to intimidate patients! Always keep your health education simple, respectful, and easy to grasp. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T10#GNS313_U1_T10_h7)

question: Why is establishing a patient baseline important during a cardiovascular assessment?

options.A: It removes the need to perform future physical examinations
options.B: It helps the nurse notice sudden changes in the patient's condition
options.C: It proves that the doctor's diagnosis is always completely correct
options.D: It lowers the overall cost of hospital admission for the client

explanation: Knowing a patient's normal state allows the nurse to quickly spot abnormal shifts that signal worsening heart trouble. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T2#GNS213_U1_T2_h1)

question: What is the primary reason nurses must master drug dosage calculations?

options.A: To reduce the workload of the hospital pharmacy
options.B: To speed up the hospital discharge process
options.C: To prevent medication errors and keep patients safe
options.D: To replace the need for physician order sheets

explanation: Accurate calculations ensure the patient receives the exact therapeutic amount, avoiding underdosing or dangerous toxicity. [learn more](GNS125_U2_T6#GNS125_U2_T6_h1)

question: A patient comes in feeling constantly exhausted, has gained weight, hates cold weather, and has dry, coarse hair. What condition do these signs point to?

options.A: Hypothyroidism
options.B: Hyperthyroidism
options.C: Cushing's syndrome
options.D: Addison's disease

explanation: You've got this! These are classic signs of a sluggish metabolism caused by not having enough thyroid hormones in the body. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T14#GNS222_U2_T14_h3)

question: What is the main purpose of tilting the X-ray table into different angles during a barium swallow?

options.A: To drain excess stomach fluids before the contrast is given
options.B: To help gravity coat the entire lining of the esophagus and stomach with barium
options.C: To prevent the patient from falling asleep during the procedure
options.D: To speed up the digestion of the barium into the bloodstream

explanation: Changing table positions ensures that the liquid barium flows over all mucosal surfaces so small defects or ulcers are not missed. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T13#GNS221_U2_T13_h4)

question: Where are our actual smell (olfactory) receptor cells located?

options.A: Inside the hard palate of the mouth
options.B: On the roof of the nasal cavity
options.C: Along the lower respiratory tract
options.D: Within the external ear canal

explanation: Spot on! The delicate olfactory epithelium holding our smell receptors sits high up near the roof of the nasal cavity, right where incoming air sweeps past. [learn more](GNS211_U4_T9#GNS211_U4_T9_h2)

question: Why does a strong primary health care system help major teaching hospitals?

options.A: It ensures that nurses never have to work night shifts again
options.B: It eliminates the need for any laboratory testing supplies
options.C: It allows doctors to retire at an early age
options.D: It prevents tertiary hospitals from becoming overwhelmed with preventable conditions

explanation: Well reasoned! When local clinics handle everyday health issues, big hospitals stay clear and ready for truly complex cases. [learn more](GNS225_U1_T7#GNS225_U1_T7_h6)

question: Why is the optic disc referred to as the blind spot?

options.A: It absorbs all incoming light
options.B: It is blocked by the iris
options.C: It lacks rods and cones
options.D: It is located outside the eye

explanation: The optic disc is where nerve fibers leave the eyeball, meaning no photoreceptor cells are present there to detect light. [learn more](GNS211_U4_T1#GNS211_U4_T1_h5)

question: Why is high blood potassium treated urgently in a patient with acute renal failure?

options.A: To encourage the kidneys to immediately start producing concentrated urine
options.B: To prevent severe infection in the upper urinary tract
options.C: To prevent dangerous and life-threatening heart rhythm changes
options.D: To stop the sudden breakdown of muscle tissue throughout the body

explanation: Elevated potassium levels severely affect the electrical system of the heart, leading to fatal cardiac arrhythmias if left untreated. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T6#GNS213_U4_T6_h5)

question: What happens to C3 complement protein levels in the blood during active Post-Streptococcal Glomerulonephritis?

options.A: They rise to very high levels
options.B: They fluctuate every few hours
options.C: They drop below normal levels
options.D: They remain completely unchanged

explanation: Think of C3 proteins as defense workers that get completely used up and depleted by the ongoing immune battle in the kidneys, leaving low levels in the blood test. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T4#GNS213_U4_T4_h5)

question: Which of these describes a normal (eutocic) labour?

options.A: Surgical induction with a breech presentation at 35 weeks
options.B: Prolonged stages requiring vacuum extraction
options.C: Preterm delivery with multiple interventions
options.D: Spontaneous onset with a cephalic presentation at term

explanation: Spot on! For labour to be truly normal, it should start on its own between 37-42 weeks, and the baby's head (cephalic) should come first. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T002#GNS226_U3_T002_h1)

question: Why is it usually best not to force extra fluids or IV drips on an actively dying patient?

options.A: It can cause fluid overload and painful swelling
options.B: It immediately speeds up the dying process
options.C: It causes severe throat infections
options.D: It completely stops the patient from feeling any pain

explanation: As the body systems slow down, they cannot process extra fluids well. This leads to swelling and congestion rather than helping the patient heal. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T12#GNS321_U4_T12_h3)

question: A mother asks what food to first give her six-month-old. What is the best nurse response?

options.A: Cow milk straight from the carton to build strong bones
options.B: Clear vegetable broths with added table salt for taste
options.C: Sweetened fruit juices to encourage quick swallowing
options.D: Thick, nutrient-dense mashed foods like iron-fortified porridge or yam

explanation: First foods should be thick and rich in nutrients, especially iron, to match the rapid growth spurt of a six-month-old baby. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T012#GNS227_U7_T012_h3)

question: What is the main goal of spermatogenesis in the male body?

options.A: Maturation of mature oocytes
options.B: Secretion of seminal fluid proteins
options.C: Production of haploid spermatozoa
options.D: Formation of diploid spermatogonia

explanation: Think of spermatogenesis as the factory process that turns immature germ cells into mature sperm cells with half the normal chromosomes, ready for fertilization! [learn more](GNS121_U4_T6#GNS121_U4_T6_h1)

question: Why do you inject air into a multi-dose medication vial before you pull out the liquid?

options.A: To kill any bacteria inside the glass vial
options.B: To dilute a medication that is too thick
options.C: To prevent a vacuum from forming inside the vial
options.D: To warm up the medication for the patient

explanation: You got it! Pumping in a little air replaces the space of the liquid you're about to take out, making the drawing process smooth and easy. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T7#GNS122_U1_T7_h4)

question: What is a major workforce challenge currently facing the long-term care industry?

options.A: An overabundance of licensed nurses competing for very few open beds
options.B: Mandatory retirement ages that force nurses to leave the field early
options.C: Severe staff shortages and high burnout rates among nurses and aides
options.D: Strict laws prohibiting nurses from working in residential settings

explanation: It's no secret that long-term care can be tough. Low pay, heavy workloads, and physical demands mean keeping and recruiting enough nurses remains a major hurdle. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T5#GNS324_U5_T5_h6)

question: Which type of receptor is primarily found on target organs of the parasympathetic nervous system?

options.A: Alpha adrenergic receptors
options.B: Beta adrenergic receptors
options.C: Muscarinic receptors
options.D: Nicotinic skeletal receptors

explanation: Parasympathetic postganglionic fibers release acetylcholine, which binds to muscarinic receptors on target effector organs. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T29#GNS211_U3_T29_h6)

question: A patient tells you they are resting at home in their own bed, but they are actually sitting in a hospital ward. How would you describe this?

options.A: Normal cognitive aging changes
options.B: Disorientation to place
options.C: Impaired immediate recall memory
options.D: A defect in cranial nerve function

explanation: When a patient doesn't realize where they physically are, we document it as disorientation to place. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T4#GNS222_U3_T4_h2)

question: A patient arrives with a deep dog puncture on their hand. After checking the ABCs, what should the nurse assess first?

options.A: The patient's current insurance and employment details
options.B: Distal pulses, motor function, and finger sensation
options.C: Whether the patient prefers oral or intravenous medication
options.D: The exact monetary value of any damaged clothing

explanation: Always check circulation, movement, and feeling early on! Deep punctures can easily cause hidden damage to nearby blood vessels and tendons. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T11#GNS221_U3_T11_h3)

question: Which anti-TB drug is known to cause vision issues like optic neuritis?

options.A: Pyrazinamide
options.B: Ethambutol
options.C: Isoniazid
options.D: Rifampicin

explanation: Ethambutol can mess with the optic nerve. That's why checking a patient's eyesight and color vision during treatment is a key nursing duty! [learn more](GNS223_U2_T6#GNS223_U2_T6_h5)

question: What happens to blood vessels when they are exposed to a lot of heat?

options.A: Vasoconstriction, which completely stops blood circulation
options.B: Thrombosis of all major pelvic arteries
options.C: Vasodilation, which increases blood flow to the area
options.D: Immediate sclerosis and permanent vessel collapse

explanation: You've got this! Heat causes blood vessels to relax and widen (vasodilation), which brings more blood flow right to that warmed area. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T15#GNS312_U1_T15_h2)

question: How does a vision statement differ from a mission statement?

options.A: A vision statement is created by junior staff, while a mission is written by the government
options.B: A vision statement looks forward to future aspirations, while a mission focuses on present purpose
options.C: A vision statement is kept secret from patients, while a mission is printed on posters
options.D: A vision statement deals strictly with daily nursing chores, while a mission covers finances

explanation: Visions describe a future desired state, whereas missions focus on what the organization is doing today. [learn more](GST321_U2_T3#GST321_U2_T3_h2)

question: Which of these is a classic physical sign that a patient is experiencing acute fear?

options.A: Slow and deep breathing
options.B: Diaphoresis and trembling
options.C: Low blood pressure
options.D: Warm and dry skin

explanation: Correct! A sudden rush of adrenaline makes the body sweat (diaphoresis) and shake when a person is deeply frightened. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T11#GNS123_U3_T11_h4)

question: What is the main goal of giving someone a vaccine?

options.A: To stimulate antibody production and memory cell formation without causing disease
options.B: To replace damaged white blood cells in immunosuppressed patients
options.C: To permanently destroy all innate immune system pathways
options.D: To provide immediate relief from acute bacterial infections

explanation: Vaccines are like practice drills for your immune system. They introduce a safe, weakened piece of a germ so your body learns the defense strategy without actually getting sick. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T14#GNS111_U2_T14_h6)

question: Why is the risk of infection often lower in home care than in hospital wards?

options.A: Homes are chemically sterilized by professional cleaning crews daily
options.B: Home care nurses wear full surgical hazmat suits during every visit
options.C: Bacteria cannot survive outside of a traditional hospital building
options.D: Patients are separated from other sick individuals and hospital germs

explanation: Recovering away from shared rooms and hospital pathogens greatly reduces the chance of catching secondary infections. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T11#GNS324_U1_T11_h4)

question: A newborn is getting PPV, but their heart rate is still 70 and their chest isn't moving. What should you check first?

options.A: Increase the oxygen concentration to 100 percent
options.B: Insert an umbilical venous catheter for epinephrine
options.C: Check and adjust the mask seal and head position
options.D: Immediately begin emergency chest compressions

explanation: If the chest isn't rising, air isn't getting in. Always check the mask seal and head position first to fix the airflow before doing anything more drastic. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T010#GNS226_U3_T010_h4)

question: If you find a patient's PMI shifted far to the left, what does that usually suggest?

options.A: Collapse of the right lung
options.B: Normal athletic heart conditioning
options.C: Dehydration and low blood volume
options.D: Enlargement of the heart

explanation: When the heart muscle gets bigger or stretched out, the PMI moves downward and outward to the left. Spotting this helps you catch complications early! [learn more](GNS112_U6_T2#GNS112_U6_T2_h7)

question: What is the most common reason people develop Wernicke encephalopathy?

options.A: A sudden head injury
options.B: A bad food allergy
options.C: Eating too much sugar
options.D: Chronic alcohol misuse

explanation: Correct! Long-term heavy alcohol use stops the gut from absorbing thiamine properly, making it the top cause of this condition. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T7#GNS222_U4_T7_h3)

question: How do environmental health challenges generally differ between urban and rural settings?

options.A: Rural areas are overcrowded while urban areas have vast open farmlands
options.B: Urban areas are completely free from any form of environmental hazards
options.C: Urban areas have more industrial pollution while rural areas face agricultural risks
options.D: Both settings experience identical levels of traffic congestion and smog

explanation: You got it! Cities deal with traffic and factories, while villages face challenges like farming chemicals or lack of clean water sources. [learn more](GNS225_U1_T2#GNS225_U1_T2_h5)

question: How are animal fats and oils usually used in traditional medicine?

options.A: As intravenous substitutes for blood plasma
options.B: As sterile eye drops for acute glaucoma
options.C: As primary replacements for oral antibiotics
options.D: As bases for topical balms and ointments

explanation: Animal fats make a nice, greasy base that helps carry healing ingredients and keeps them sticking to the skin to soothe pain or swelling. [learn more](GNS125_U2_T2#GNS125_U2_T2_h4)

question: Which of these is NOT a typical complication of intraperitoneal administration?

options.A: Catheter blockage
options.B: Peritonitis
options.C: Abdominal pain
options.D: Inhalation pneumonia

explanation: Correct! Inhalation pneumonia is a lung issue, so it's not a direct local complication of accessing the peritoneal belly cavity. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T11#GNS125_U3_T11_h6)

question: Which type of nursing standard focuses directly on the environment and available resources?

options.A: Financial standards
options.B: Structure standards
options.C: Process standards
options.D: Outcome standards

explanation: Structure standards look at the physical setup, tools, and staffing numbers needed before care even begins. [learn more](GST321_U1_T20#GST321_U1_T20_h2)

question: What is the medicalisation of FGM?

options.A: Using modern local anesthesia during traditional FGM rites
options.B: Performing FGM using trained healthcare workers in clinical settings
options.C: Treating the physical complications of FGM in a hospital
options.D: Researching surgical ways to reverse FGM damage

explanation: Medicalisation refers to health professionals performing the procedure under the false assumption that clinical hygiene removes the harm. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T5#GNS312_U1_T5_h1)

question: Why is proper documentation of a referral important for the client's care?

options.A: It proves to the government that the nurse worked extra hours
options.B: It prevents the receiving facility from repeating unnecessary assessments
options.C: It allows the nurse to charge extra administrative fees to the client
options.D: It stops the client from ever returning to the primary health center

explanation: Clear notes on clinical history and vital signs save time and guide the receiving team straight to appropriate management. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T029#GNS226_U6_T029_h5)

question: Which of these side-to-side measurements is the wider one across a baby's skull?

options.A: The biparietal diameter
options.B: The bitemporal diameter
options.C: Neither is used in obstetrics
options.D: Both measure exactly the same

explanation: The biparietal diameter stretches across the widest part of the parietal bones, making it broader than the bitemporal measurement across the temples. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T13#GNS121_U6_T13_h4)

question: How is a patient positioned when they are in the supine position?

options.A: Flat on their abdomen
options.B: On their side with top knee flexed
options.C: Flat on their back
options.D: Sitting up at a 90-degree angle

explanation: The supine position means lying horizontally on the back, facing upward. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T8#GNS112_U4_T8_h2)

question: How does Behavioural Change Communication (BCC) differ from basic health education?

options.A: BCC focuses on active behavior change rather than just sharing information
options.B: Basic health education involves no communication at all
options.C: BCC is only used inside tertiary hospitals by doctors
options.D: Basic education is meant for children while BCC is for adults

explanation: Think of it this way: health education gives people the facts, but BCC goes a step further to help them actually overcome personal and social barriers to take action. You're building solid community nursing foundations! [learn more](GNS124_U5_T8#GNS124_U5_T8_h1)

question: A mum on her second day after delivery hasn't passed stool and is scared to use the toilet. What is the best nursing action?

options.A: Withhold all oral fluids and food until she passes flatus
options.B: Administer a strong stimulant enema immediately without consulting a doctor
options.C: Insist that she remains in bed until her bowel movement happens naturally
options.D: Encourage fluid intake, walking around, and check if stool softeners were ordered

explanation: Gentle movement, plenty of fluids, and stool softeners are the safest, kindest way to help her first postpartum toilet trip go smoothly! [learn more](GNS121_U7_T4#GNS121_U7_T4_h8)

question: When is the standard comprehensive postnatal check usually scheduled after the initial hospital stay?

options.A: At one year
options.B: At six months
options.C: At six weeks
options.D: At two weeks

explanation: The six-week postnatal visit is the big milestone where we check that both the mother's body and mind have fully recovered from pregnancy and birth. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T016#GNS226_U3_T016_h9)

question: Why should nurses team up with traditional and religious leaders in community campaigns against GBV?

options.A: Because traditional leaders provide direct funding for hospital equipment
options.B: Because these leaders hold significant influence in shaping community norms and attitudes
options.C: Because religious leaders take over medical duties during emergencies
options.D: Because nurses are not legally permitted to speak publicly outside hospitals

explanation: Well done! Community leaders are respected voices; partnering with them helps change cultural attitudes and gets people on board with prevention. [learn more](GNS312_U4_T8#GNS312_U4_T8_h9)

question: How many loose or watery stools in a day is generally used to define diarrhoea?

options.A: Seven or more mucous stools per day
options.B: Five or more solid stools per day
options.C: Three or more loose stools per day
options.D: One or two hard stools per day

explanation: Passing three or more loose or watery bowel movements within 24 hours is the standard clinical sign that someone has diarrhoea. You've got this! [learn more](GNS212_U1_T7#GNS212_U1_T7_h1)

question: What is the main job of the autonomic nervous system?

options.A: Transmitting sensory signals from the skin
options.B: Regulating involuntary body functions
options.C: Processing conscious thought and memory
options.D: Controlling voluntary skeletal muscles

explanation: Think of the autonomic system as your body's autopilot. It takes care of internal organs and smooth muscles automatically so you don't have to consciously tell your heart to beat or your food to digest! [learn more](GNS211_U3_T5#GNS211_U3_T5_h1)

question: How does buprenorphine help a patient recovering from an opioid addiction?

options.A: It acts as a partial agonist to reduce cravings without causing strong euphoria
options.B: It puts the patient into an immediate artificial sleep until withdrawal ends
options.C: It causes severe vomiting whenever the patient tries to use illegal drugs
options.D: It permanently destroys all opioid receptors in the brain

explanation: Buprenorphine satisfies brain receptors enough to prevent withdrawal and cravings, but its partial action prevents a dangerous high. [learn more](GNS125_U2_T12#GNS125_U2_T12_h7)

question: A nurse suspects a patient's injuries are from domestic abuse, but the patient is too scared to talk. What should the nurse do first?

options.A: Provide a safe, private environment and gently encourage the patient to talk
options.B: Ignore the suspicion because the patient did not report it directly
options.C: Discharge the patient quickly to avoid getting involved in legal matters
options.D: Call the police immediately and force the patient to make a public statement

explanation: Wonderful! Building trust in a warm, confidential space gives frightened patients the courage to open up at their own pace. [learn more](GNS312_U4_T14#GNS312_U4_T14_h8)

question: What is a major clinical advantage of Long-Acting Reversible Contraception (LARC) over regular daily pills?

options.A: They completely eliminate all risks of hormonal side effects
options.B: They do not rely on daily user adherence to remain effective
options.C: They can be inserted and removed safely at home by the patient
options.D: They provide automatic protection against viral and bacterial STIs

explanation: LARC methods (like implants or coils) take away the stress of remembering a daily pill. Once they're in, they work quietly in the background for years! [learn more](GNS215_U6_T17#GNS215_U6_T17_h5)

question: Why is it so important to report an accidental needle-stick or blood exposure immediately?

options.A: Post-exposure preventative treatments work best when started quickly
options.B: Agency managers need time to discipline the careless worker
options.C: Insurance companies will refuse claims filed after twenty-four hours
options.D: State laws make late reporting a criminal offense for nurses

explanation: Time matters! Preventive medicines for bloodborne infections like HIV or Hepatitis B work best when taken very soon after an exposure. [learn more](GNS324_U6_T9#GNS324_U6_T9_h8)

question: Why does the examiner systematically trace the retinal blood vessel branches during the assessment?

options.A: To push any trapped fluid away from the delicate optic nerve head
options.B: To measure the exact pulse rate of blood flowing through the brain
options.C: To check for normal branching patterns, caliber changes, and color
options.D: To stimulate the retina into producing more natural lubricating tears

explanation: Tracing the vessels helps the clinician spot abnormalities like vessel narrowing, crossing changes, or hemorrhages associated with systemic disease. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T8#GNS221_U2_T8_h7)

question: A patient has acute Hepatitis B. Which part of their history helps you trace how they caught it?

options.A: Swimming in a public pool with high chlorine levels
options.B: Eating unwashed raw vegetables from a local market stall
options.C: Receiving an unscreened blood transfusion or sharing needles
options.D: Drinking untreated well water during a rural community visit

explanation: Spot on! Hepatitis B is a bloodborne infection, meaning it spreads through contact with infected blood or sharp objects like needles and unsterilized blades. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T16#GNS313_U2_T16_h2)

question: Who is widely recognized as the pioneer of modern professional nursing?

options.A: Mary Seacole
options.B: Linda Richards
options.C: Clara Barton
options.D: Florence Nightingale

explanation: Florence Nightingale transformed nursing during the Crimean War by emphasizing sanitation, organization, and formal training. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T1#GNS112_U1_T1_h2)

question: Which condition involves inflammation of the organ that makes lipase for fat digestion?

options.A: Gastritis
options.B: Cystitis
options.C: Pancreatitis
options.D: Appendicitis

explanation: Pancreatitis is inflammation of the pancreas—the vital organ that pumps out lipase and other enzymes to digest fats. [learn more](GNS227_U6_T005#GNS227_U6_T005_h4)

question: What is the main goal of keeping a patient clean and fresh?

options.A: To shorten the hospital stay
options.B: To protect skin and stop infections
options.C: To cover up unpleasant room smells
options.D: To boost body metabolism

explanation: Well done! Keeping skin clean stops it from breaking down and keeps out harmful germs. You've got this! [learn more](GNS324_U6_T2#GNS324_U6_T2_h1)

question: Which of these is counted as a healthy food group in standard dietary scoring?

options.A: Dark green leafy vegetables
options.B: Carbonated soft drinks
options.C: Processed table sugar
options.D: Artificial food flavorings

explanation: That's right! Ugwu, spinach, and other dark greens are packed with essential nutrients like iron and folate to keep the body strong. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T004#GNS227_U2_T004_h2)

question: Where in the brain do generalized seizures start?

options.A: A localized spot in one hemisphere
options.B: Only the frontal lobe
options.C: The brainstem exclusively
options.D: Both hemispheres simultaneously

explanation: Well done! Generalized seizures involve electrical activity spreading across both sides of the brain right from the start. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T10#GNS222_U4_T10_h3)

question: Why do we divide an operating suite into unrestricted, semi-restricted, and restricted zones?

options.A: To progressively lower the risk of microbial contamination closer to the patient
options.B: To ensure that doctors and nurses have separate break rooms
options.C: To make it easier to clean the floors with automated machines
options.D: To prevent patients from wandering into the administrative offices

explanation: You got it! These zoning layers act like security checkpoints, filtering out dust and germs step-by-step before anyone steps near the patient. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T2#GNS123_U5_T2_h6)

question: Who played the primary role in introducing Western-style nursing and hospitals to Nigeria during the colonial era?

options.A: Missionary societies
options.B: Military combat units
options.C: International trade unions
options.D: Local traditional rulers

explanation: Christian missions established the earliest Western hospitals and introduced formal nursing concepts to Nigeria. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T2#GNS112_U1_T2_h4)

question: External rotation of the baby's head is actually caused by the turning of which body part?

options.A: The shoulders
options.B: The feet
options.C: The hips
options.D: The chest

explanation: Exactly! As the baby's shoulders twist inside to fit the pelvis, that movement travels up the neck and makes the head turn on the outside. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T005#GNS226_U3_T005_h6)

question: Which professional group is NOT part of the healthcare team managing suspected elder abuse?

options.A: Home healthcare nurses
options.B: Astronaut training coordinators
options.C: Medical social workers
options.D: Primary care physicians

explanation: Rocket science has no place here—multidisciplinary teams for elder care involve nurses, doctors, and social workers! [learn more](GNS324_U3_T10#GNS324_U3_T10_h6)

question: What is the most common underlying cause of postpartum hemorrhage?

options.A: Retained placenta
options.B: Coagulation failure
options.C: Uterine atony
options.D: Vaginal tearing

explanation: Uterine atony happens when the muscle of the uterus fails to contract properly after delivery, leaving open blood vessels that bleed heavily. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T015#GNS226_U1_T015_h2)

question: Which type of child maltreatment happens most often?

options.A: Emotional abuse
options.B: Neglect
options.C: Sexual abuse
options.D: Physical abuse

explanation: Failing to provide basic needs and proper supervision is sadly the most common form of child maltreatment we see. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T24#GNS225_U5_T24_h2)

question: A patient with chronic bronchitis and a lot of phlegm asks for a strong cough suppressant. How should you respond?

options.A: Suggest stopping all other respiratory medications immediately.
options.B: Recommend mixing the cough syrup with warm milk for faster absorption.
options.C: Advise taking a double dose of the medication right before bedtime.
options.D: Explain that suppressing the cough could cause mucus to build up dangerously in the lungs.

question: Which nursing action helps ensure an accurate blood pressure reading during a screening clinic?

options.A: Using a cuff that is much smaller than the patient's arm circumference
options.B: Allowing the patient to chat actively while the cuff inflates
options.C: Taking the measurement immediately after the patient jogs up the stairs

options.C: Leave the open hole uncovered to let the remaining fluid drain out
options.D: Put sterile gloves on and push the tube right back into the wound

explanation: Placing a sterile dressing over the hole protects the exposed tissue from bacteria, and you should never reinsert a fallen drain because it is no longer sterile. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T14#GNS122_U2_T14_h6)

question: Why are day care centres particularly vulnerable to infectious disease outbreaks?

options.A: Clients live permanently inside the building
options.B: Groups of vulnerable individuals gather in close contact
options.C: Staff members are not allowed to wash their hands
options.D: Sanitation guidelines forbid the use of soap and water

explanation: Gathering young children or frail adults in enclosed spaces makes it easy for germs to spread rapidly among them. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T7#GNS225_U4_T7_h4)

question: Why is a multidisciplinary team (doctors, nurses, physiotherapists) so important for patients with advanced disseminated sclerosis?

options.A: Physicians are not permitted to manage neurological disorders alone
options.B: The disease affects many different physical, cognitive, and emotional functions
options.C: It eliminates the need for any ongoing medical drug therapy
options.D: Patients require daily surgical procedures to replace damaged nerves

explanation: Because MS touches movement, speech, mood, and daily living, it takes a whole team of specialists working together to give the patient the best quality of life. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T3#GNS222_U4_T3_h8)

question: Which of these is a reliable way for a nurse to check if a patient is really taking their drugs?

options.A: Conducting pill counts and reviewing pharmacy refill logs
options.B: Trusting that the patient remembers all dosing schedules accurately
options.C: Assuming compliance if the patient smiles during clinic visits
options.D: Asking family members if they think the patient looks healthy

explanation: Numbers don't lie! Pill counts and pharmacy records give us solid proof of whether the medicine is actually leaving the container. [learn more](GNS215_U4_T3#GNS215_U4_T3_h5)

question: What is the main reason we give folic acid supplements to women in early pregnancy?

options.A: To accelerate infant tooth eruption
options.B: To lower maternal blood pressure
options.C: To prevent neural tube defects
options.D: To stop excessive morning sickness

explanation: Folic acid taken before and during early pregnancy helps protect the baby's developing brain and spinal cord. Super important vitamin! [learn more](GNS226_U1_T006#GNS226_U1_T006_h6)

question: Why are schools considered great spots for public health interventions?

options.A: Schools have unlimited financial resources to buy medical equipment
options.B: Teachers possess advanced clinical degrees in nursing and medicine
options.C: Students are legally required to receive medical treatment at school
options.D: Children spend a large portion of their formative years gathered in one place

explanation: Spot on! When children are gathered in one learning spot, public health workers can easily reach many of them at once to build healthy habits. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T2#GNS225_U4_T2_h1)

question: Where exactly are sperm cells made inside the testes?

options.A: Prostate capsule
options.B: Leydig cells
options.C: Seminiferous tubules
options.D: Bulbourethral glands

explanation: Inside the testes, you will find tiny, coiled little tubes called seminiferous tubules. That is where all the sperm production magic happens! [learn more](GNS121_U4_T2#GNS121_U4_T2_h2)

question: What is the best bed position to set a patient in before you feed them?

options.A: 45 degrees
options.B: 90 degrees
options.C: 30 degrees
options.D: 15 degrees

explanation: Sitting them straight up (High Fowler's at 90 degrees) lets gravity do the hard work, pulling food safely down the esophagus instead of toward the airway. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T7#GNS112_U5_T7_h3)

question: A ward manager in a public hospital faces severe supply shortages and staff burnout. What is the best way to handle this leadership challenge?

options.A: Waiting passively for central government authorities to fix all facility problems
options.B: Strictly punishing staff members whenever minor supply miscounts occur
options.C: Using adaptive authority to build consensus, mentor staff, and solve problems creatively
options.D: Ignoring hospital protocols entirely and letting junior nurses run the ward

explanation: When resources are tight, great leaders don't just punish—they lean on teamwork, mentor each other, and find creative local solutions to keep caring for patients. [learn more](GST321_U1_T16#GST321_U1_T16_h7)

question: Medication errors rise because a new drug pump has a confusing keypad. What is the best corrective action?

options.A: Suspending all medication administration duties for junior nurses
options.B: Decreasing the number of patients assigned to each shift nurse
options.C: Issuing official written warning letters to every nurse on the ward
options.D: Redesigning the workflow and retraining all nurses on the new keypad

explanation: Since the equipment itself is the problem, proper training and workflow adjustments directly fix the root cause. [learn more](GST321_U1_T19#GST321_U1_T19_h6)

question: A staff nurse sets a personal goal to use the SBAR communication tool during every patient handover this week. What level of objective is this?

options.A: Mission statement apex objective
options.B: Strategic executive objective
options.C: Long-term fiscal objective
options.D: Individual and operational objective

explanation: Daily practice goals set for a specific staff member fall at the base of the objective hierarchy. [learn more](GST321_U2_T3#GST321_U2_T3_h5)

question: What is a very common cause of a large bowel obstruction?

options.A: Eating too much high-fiber food at one meal
options.B: A mild viral stomach flu causing diarrhea
options.C: An overgrowth of normal intestinal bacteria
options.D: Colorectal cancer or a twisted bowel loop

explanation: Correct! Tumors growing inside the colon or a loop of bowel twisting on itself (volvulus) are major physical reasons the large intestine gets blocked. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T9#GNS213_U3_T9_h7)

question: According to Erik Erikson, what is the main psychological challenge teenagers face?

options.A: Initiative versus guilt
options.B: Identity versus role confusion
options.C: Generativity versus stagnation
options.D: Trust versus mistrust

explanation: Spot on! Teens are constantly figuring out the big question: 'Who am I and where do I fit in?' This is identity versus role confusion. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T2#GNS312_U3_T2_h6)

question: Why do family members often encourage pregnant women to follow strict local food rules?

options.A: To prevent complications like a baby growing too large for a normal delivery
options.B: To reserve expensive food items exclusively for the village elders
options.C: To ensure the mother maintains a high level of physical fitness
options.D: To comply with modern international nutritional guidelines

explanation: You got it! Most food taboos come from well-meaning family members trying to keep the baby small so delivery will be easier. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T1#GNS312_U1_T1_h4)

question: Which of these items is NOT safe or recommended for hospital waste handlers to wear?

options.A: Open-toe sandals for comfort
options.B: Heavy-duty utility gloves
options.C: Sturdy closed shoes or boots
options.D: Protective plastic aprons

explanation: Spot on! Open shoes leave feet exposed to falling sharps, chemical spills, and heavy equipment. Always wear closed shoes on duty! [learn more](GNS122_U5_T4#GNS122_U5_T4_h7)

question: When a patient with a throat infection develops a high fever, tiredness, and swollen neck glands, what do these show?

options.A: Lower airway collapse
options.B: Systemic response to the infection
options.C: Permanent vocal cord damage
options.D: Localized allergic rhinitis

explanation: Spot on! Fever and swollen lymph glands are signs that the whole body's immune system is active and fighting the germs. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T3#GNS213_U2_T3_h3)

question: What is craniosynostosis?

options.A: The premature fusion of skull sutures restricting brain growth
options.B: The temporary bulging of the soft spot during a fever
options.C: The delayed closure of fontanelles due to vitamin deficiency
options.D: The accumulation of fluid in the ventricles of the brain

explanation: Spot on! Craniosynostosis happens when the skull bones fuse together way too early, which can crowd the growing brain. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T12#GNS121_U6_T12_h7)

question: What is the main purpose of a community diagnosis?

options.A: To test new pharmaceutical drugs on healthy volunteers
options.B: To manage the financial budget of a primary health clinic
options.C: To treat individual patients in a hospital ward
options.D: To assess the overall health status and needs of a population

explanation: A community diagnosis looks broadly at an entire group of people to find out their health problems, resources, and needs rather than focusing on just one patient. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T4#GNS124_U3_T4_h1)

question: Which of the following is NOT a blockage-related (post-testicular) cause of male infertility?

options.A: Blocked vas deferens
options.B: Congenital absence of the sperm ducts
options.C: Epididymal scarring from infection
options.D: Klinefelter syndrome

explanation: Klinefelter syndrome is a chromosomal condition affecting the testes, whereas the other options are physical blockages in the tubes that carry sperm. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T13#GNS311_U1_T13_h5)

question: What is an important duty of a community health nurse when dealing with voluntary agencies?

options.A: Referring vulnerable patients to appropriate agency programs
options.B: Managing the global headquarters of faith-based charities
options.C: Auditing the financial tax accounts of all international donors
options.D: Passing new national legislation for non-profit groups

explanation: Correct! As a nurse, knowing what local agencies offer helps you connect your patients to free or low-cost support outside the hospital. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T28#GNS225_U5_T28_h8)

question: How does a rehab facility differ from a regular acute care hospital ward?

options.A: Rehab facilities deal strictly with infectious diseases, while acute care wards handle surgeries.
options.B: Rehab facilities prohibit family visitation to protect the therapy schedule.
options.C: Acute care hospitals do not employ registered nurses, whereas rehab facilities are nurse-run.
options.D: Acute care focuses on life-saving stabilization, while rehab focuses on restoring functional independence.

explanation: Spot on! Acute care handles the active crisis, while rehab steps in once the patient is stable enough to focus on long-term recovery and therapy. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T10#GNS324_U5_T10_h1)

question: Why is severe anemia especially dangerous for a woman going into labor?

options.A: She has very little reserve to survive normal blood loss during delivery
options.B: She will automatically develop eclampsia within hours
options.C: Her contractions will completely stop during the first stage
options.D: Her baby will be born with severe bone deformities

explanation: You're doing great! Every delivery involves some blood loss. A mom with low blood levels (anemia) cannot afford even a small loss without sliding into shock. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T014#GNS226_U1_T014_h4)

question: How can a nurse manager use descriptive research on patient admission rates?

options.A: To eliminate the need for any further hospital documentation
options.B: To plan adequate staffing levels and shift rosters for busy periods
options.C: To test a new surgical procedure on incoming emergency patients
options.D: To prove that nurses cause patient illnesses during night shifts

explanation: Knowing peak admission times helps nurse managers schedule enough hands on deck so the ward runs smoothly and patients get great care. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T9#GNS224_U1_T9_h8)

question: What do anticoagulant medications actually do in the body?

options.A: Make the circulating blood thicker
options.B: Dissolve existing blood clots completely
options.C: Stop platelets from clumping together
options.D: Prevent the formation of new blood clots

explanation: Think of anticoagulants as your body's stop sign for new clots. They don't break down clots that are already there, but they stop new ones from forming or getting bigger! [learn more](GNS223_U1_T5#GNS223_U1_T5_h1)

question: When listening to music, what property of a sound wave tells you whether the note is high or low (pitch)?

options.A: Resonance
options.B: Frequency
options.C: Amplitude
options.D: Velocity

explanation: Frequency is measured in hertz and determines the pitch of a sound. Think of high-frequency sounds as high-pitched, like a baby crying, and low-frequency as deep, like a drum! [learn more](GNS211_U4_T7#GNS211_U4_T7_h1)

question: Which emotional reaction is very common in patients right after they acquire a physical disability?

options.A: Complete indifference and forgetfulness
options.B: Grief, shock, and depression
options.C: Aggressive pursuit of extreme sports
options.D: Immediate acceptance and joy

explanation: Losing bodily function triggers a deep grief process, much like losing a loved one. Shock and depression are very normal initial responses. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T16#GNS225_U5_T16_h6)

question: In what year was the historic Alma-Ata Declaration on Primary Health Care adopted?
explanation: The landmark international conference that defined Primary Health Care took place in Alma-Ata in 1978. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T4#GNS124_U1_T4_h1)

question: Why is the hypodermis so important for protecting your bones and muscles?

options.A: It contains active stem cells that repair bone fractures
options.B: It acts as a physical shock absorber against trauma
options.C: It generates sweat to cool deep tissues during exercise
options.D: It produces keratin to harden the surface against impacts

explanation: Spot on! The layer of fat cushions bumps and blows, protecting the delicate muscles and bones underneath. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T1#GNS213_U5_T1_h4)

question: Why do some women delay seeking medical care for incomplete abortions in local communities?

options.A: Automatic recovery without intervention in nearly all septic cases
options.B: Lack of interest in recovering from physical weakness or bleeding
options.C: Strict government regulations that ban women from leaving their homes
options.D: Fear of social stigma, legal repercussions, and judgment from healthcare workers

explanation: True. Fear of harsh treatment by hospital staff or society stops many women from seeking timely care. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T021#GNS226_U5_T021_h6)

question: A patient needs help managing their diet, exercise, and chronic illness. What type of counselling is best?

options.A: Health and lifestyle counselling
options.B: Vocational counselling
options.C: Career placement guidance
options.D: Educational guidance

explanation: When the focus is on daily habits like eating well and staying active to manage a condition, it's health and lifestyle counselling! [learn more](GNS124_U5_T11#GNS124_U5_T11_h4)

question: During the dry season in northern Nigeria, a patient presents with a very stiff neck, high fever, and confusion. What should you suspect first?

options.A: Simple malaria fever
options.B: Cerebrospinal meningitis
options.C: Severe cholera infection
options.D: Typhoid fever illness

explanation: Spot on! A stiff neck and high fever are classic warning signs of meningitis, which tends to cause seasonal outbreaks in northern Nigeria during the dry season. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T15#GNS313_U1_T15_h4)

question: Why is understanding how drug classes work so important for patient safety?

options.A: It ensures the hospital pharmacy never runs out of stock
options.B: It allows nurses to manufacture replacement drugs at the nursing station
options.C: It replaces the need to check patient identification bands
options.D: It helps nurses anticipate overlapping side effects and drug interactions

explanation: Knowing drug classes helps you spot dangerous drug combinations or double-up side effects before they cause harm. [learn more](GNS125_U2_T4#GNS125_U2_T4_h8)

question: In many poor communities, what is the main dietary cause of micronutrient deficiencies?

options.A: High intake of dairy products and fresh vegetables
options.B: Frequent eating of high-protein animal meals
options.C: Heavy reliance on a single starchy staple food
options.D: Excessive consumption of imported canned foods

explanation: Correct! Eating only one starchy food day in and day out means the body misses out on the wide variety of nutrients it needs. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T7#GNS313_U3_T7_h3)

question: What is the main goal of palliative care?

options.A: Providing financial aid to grieving families
options.B: Curing the underlying terminal disease completely
options.C: Speeding up the natural dying process safely
options.D: Improving the quality of life for patients and families

explanation: Think of palliative care as a comforting blanket. Its main goal is to bring peace, ease pain, and support both the patient and their loved ones through a tough time. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T2#GNS321_U4_T2_h1)

question: Why might a patient with a left atrial myxoma suddenly faint when changing body position?

options.A: The tumour causes a sudden drop in the patient's body temperature
options.B: The heart muscle instantly grows twice its normal size
options.C: The mobile tumour temporarily plugs up the mitral valve, stopping blood flow
options.D: The patient's lungs stop taking in oxygen due to an allergic reaction

explanation: Some tumours hang on a little stalk. When the patient moves, the tumour can swing over and block the valve like a cork in a bottle, cutting off blood supply and causing fainting. Fascinating clinical detail! [learn more](GNS213_U1_T8#GNS213_U1_T8_h4)

question: Which substance serves as the main chemical building block for steroid hormones?

options.A: Tyrosine
options.B: Glucose
options.C: Nucleic acids
options.D: Cholesterol

explanation: Steroid hormones are made straight from cholesterol! Even though people often talk about cholesterol in a bad nutritional light, our bodies actually need it to build vital hormones. [learn more](GNS211_U1_T10#GNS211_U1_T10_h2)

question: What does a nurse typically see during an otoscopic exam of a patient with acute ear infection (otitis media)?

options.A: A clear, translucent eardrum with a sharp cone of light
options.B: A dark perforated hole with dry flaky skin inside the canal
options.C: A bulging, bright red tympanic membrane with obscured landmarks
options.D: A completely pale, flat membrane with prominent bone outlines

explanation: When pus builds up behind the eardrum from an infection, it pushes the drum outward and turns it very red, hiding the normal landmarks. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T3#GNS221_U2_T3_h7)

question: What is the simplest way families can kill germs in drinking water at home?

options.A: Filtration
options.B: Boiling
options.C: Freezing
options.D: Sedimentation

explanation: That's right! Bringing water to a rolling boil is a quick, reliable way to kill disease-causing organisms right in your kitchen. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T9#GNS112_U5_T9_h3)

question: What is a recommended eating pattern to help reduce nausea during early pregnancy?

options.A: Eating small, frequent meals throughout the day
options.B: Eating three large meals loaded with healthy fats
options.C: Fasting until the afternoon to let the stomach rest
options.D: Drinking a large glass of water right before every meal

explanation: Keeping a little food in the stomach prevents the empty-stomach feeling that often worsens nausea. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T012#GNS226_U2_T012_h4)

question: Why do we schedule baby clinic visits as a regular routine instead of just a one-off appointment?

options.A: To ensure mothers stay inside the clinic building for several hours
options.B: To track steady growth patterns and catch developmental issues early
options.C: To prevent mothers from visiting traditional birth attendants
options.D: To keep vaccine vials open and cold until the next clinic day

explanation: You got it! Seeing a baby regularly lets us watch their growth over time and catch any small health or developmental issues early. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T2#GNS225_U3_T2_h1)

question: When is an exchange transfusion chosen over standard phototherapy?

options.A: When bilirubin levels are critically high and threatening the brain
options.B: When the baby develops a mild diaper rash during light treatment
options.C: When the baby has mild jaundice lasting longer than two weeks
options.D: When the mother wants to formula feed instead of breastfeeding

explanation: An exchange transfusion is an emergency procedure used when bilirubin levels are dangerously high, quickly swapping the baby's blood to protect their brain. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T017#GNS226_U3_T017_h7)

question: What is the main goal of a Drug Revolving Fund (DRF) in a hospital?

options.A: To ensure a continuous supply of affordable essential drugs
options.B: To provide free medical care to all indigent citizens
options.C: To fund the construction of new hospital wards and buildings
options.D: To generate heavy profits for the hospital management board

explanation: Think of the DRF as a self-sustaining cycle. Its main job is to make sure essential drugs never run out in the hospital pharmacy, so patients can always get what they need at a fair price! [learn more](GNS215_U3_T1#GNS215_U3_T1_h1)

question: What is the main purpose of a neonatal bag-valve-mask (BVM) in your kit?

options.A: To give artificial breaths to a newborn who isn't breathing on their own
options.B: To clear meconium out of the baby's tummy during a checkup
options.C: To weigh the baby accurately in kilograms
options.D: To wrap the baby securely against cold drafts

explanation: The BVM lets you gently give lifesaving breaths to a struggling newborn until they start breathing all by themselves. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T10#GNS225_U3_T10_h7)

question: Which nursing action is best for keeping track of a patient's ongoing nutrition?

options.A: Prescribing high-protein dietary supplements independently
options.B: Measuring indirect calorimetry on every single shift
options.C: Calculating precise basal metabolic rate without a formula
options.D: Recording daily weights and monitoring food intake

explanation: Never underestimate the basics! Daily weight checks and watching how much food actually gets eaten give nurses the best clues on nutritional health. [learn more](GNS227_U1_T014#GNS227_U1_T014_h7)

question: An endometrioma happens when which of the following occurs?

options.A: Ovarian surface cells multiply and produce thick mucus
options.B: The corpus luteum traps blood inside its cavity after ovulation
options.C: Uterine lining tissue grows on the outside of the ovary
options.D: An unruptured egg follicle swells excessively with clear fluid

explanation: Think of endometriomas (often called chocolate cysts!) as happening when tissue similar to the lining of the uterus decides to grow outside on the ovaries. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T32#GNS216_U5_T32_h2)

question: Which connective tissue layer wraps around an entire skeletal muscle?

options.A: Perimysium
options.B: Periosteum
options.C: Endomysium
options.D: Epimysium

explanation: Think of the epimysium as the tough outer coat that wraps up the whole muscle, keeping it safe and secure! [learn more](GNS121_U3_T9#GNS121_U3_T9_h2)

question: How do typical skin lesions of Kaposi sarcoma look?

options.A: Painful, red ulcers with a yellow base
options.B: Itchy, fluid-filled vesicular clusters
options.C: Scaly, silvery plaques with dry edges
options.D: Painless, purplish or brownish nodules

explanation: Skin lesions from Kaposi sarcoma usually show up as distinct, firm, and painless spots or bumps that look purple, pink, or brown. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T13#GNS216_U6_T13_h3)

question: Why is physical therapy so important for a client with a progressive muscle-wasting disorder?

options.A: It replaces the need for any medications or assistive devices.
options.B: It cures the genetic defect causing the muscle weakness.
options.C: It rebuilds destroyed muscle fibers back to their original strength.
options.D: It helps maintain joint flexibility and prevents painful contractures.

explanation: Gentle stretching and range-of-motion exercises keep joints flexible and prevent muscles and tendons from painfully shortening. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T15#GNS222_U4_T15_h5)

question: After a patient has an upper endoscopy, what is the most important nursing check before giving them water?

options.A: Administering a large meal immediately to test stomach tolerance
options.B: Checking for active bowel sounds every fifteen minutes
options.C: Keeping the patient flat on their back for at least six hours
options.D: Confirming that the patient's gag reflex has returned before offering fluids

explanation: Spot on! The throat spray numbs the back of the throat, so we must wait for the gag reflex to come back to prevent them from choking on water. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T6#GNS213_U3_T6_h5)

question: Where is the limbic system located in the brain?

options.A: Inside the hollow cavities of the cerebellum
options.B: At the very front tip of the frontal lobes
options.C: On the outer surface of the occipital lobe
options.D: Deep inside the brain surrounding the brainstem

explanation: Spot on! The structures making up the limbic system sit deep inside, wrapping around the top of the brainstem right beneath the outer cortex. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T13#GNS211_U3_T13_h1)

question: A staff nurse wants to learn advanced wound care techniques and earn a promotion to ward sister. What do these desires represent?

options.A: Statutory penalties
options.B: Financial liabilities
options.C: Personal objectives
options.D: Organisational mandates

explanation: Spot on! Wanting to learn new skills and climb the career ladder are classic examples of personal goals you set for your own nursing career. [learn more](GST321_U2_T2#GST321_U2_T2_h2)

question: Which of these is a major red flag and established risk factor for postpartum haemorrhage?

options.A: A history of previous postpartum haemorrhage
options.B: Delivery of a single low birth weight baby
options.C: Maternal age under 20 years
options.D: A very short first stage of labour

explanation: If a mother had PPH in a past delivery, she has a higher chance of experiencing it again. Always check her past obstetric history during admission! [learn more](GNS226_U4_T012#GNS226_U4_T012_h3)

question: A nurse needs to draw medication from a multidose vial for another patient. Which of these actions is unsafe?

options.A: Swabbing the rubber top of the vial with an alcohol wipe before piercing
options.B: Using a brand new, sterile syringe and needle for drawing up the dose
options.C: Checking the expiration date printed on the label of the vial
options.D: Leaving a previously used dispensing needle inserted in the vial rubber septum

explanation: Never leave a needle stuck inside a multidose vial! It acts like an open door for bacteria to crawl inside and contaminate the medicine for the next patient. [learn more](GNS122_U4_T4#GNS122_U4_T4_h2)

question: A charge nurse expects more malaria cases during the rainy season and adds extra staff early. What management function is this?

options.A: Budgeting
options.B: Controlling
options.C: Planning
options.D: Delegating

explanation: Spotting future needs ahead of time and getting ready for them is the definition of planning. You're thinking like a true nurse leader! [learn more](GST321_U1_T2#GST321_U1_T2_h2)

question: Why does semen briefly thicken right after ejaculation before turning watery again?

options.A: To prevent the sperm from leaking out immediately
options.B: To block the urinary bladder completely
options.C: To make the sperm travel much faster through the testes
options.D: To kill off any weak sperm cells present in the fluid

explanation: The initial clotting keeps everything securely in place, and then it liquefies so the sperm can start their journey upward. Clever design! [learn more](GNS121_U4_T2#GNS121_U4_T2_h6)

question: Which two organs are most commonly affected by hydatid cysts in the human body?

options.A: Liver and lungs
options.B: Heart and spleen
options.C: Stomach and pancreas
options.D: Brain and kidneys

explanation: The liver acts as the first major capillary filter for blood returning from the intestines, making it the most common site, with the lungs second. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T25#GNS313_U2_T25_h5)

question: Which of these is a classic sign of postpartum endometritis (infection of the uterus lining)?

options.A: Sudden weight gain and facial swelling
options.B: Foul-smelling lochia and fever
options.C: High blood pressure and visual changes
options.D: Painful urination and flank pain

explanation: When the uterine lining gets infected, it usually lets you know through fever, tenderness, and vaginal discharge that smells unusual or foul. You're building great clinical instincts! [learn more](GNS226_U3_T016#GNS226_U3_T016_h5)

question: A patient taking an estrogen antagonist for breast cancer complains of hot flashes. What is the best nursing response?

options.A: Document that the patient is allergic to the prescribed chemotherapy
options.B: Tell the patient to take extra birth control pills to replace the lost hormones
options.C: Advise the patient to stop taking the medication immediately because it is toxic
options.D: Explain that these symptoms often occur because the medication successfully blocks hormone receptors

explanation: Reassure your patient! Side effects like hot flashes happen because the drug is doing its job by blocking estrogen activity all over the body. [learn more](GNS211_U1_T11#GNS211_U1_T11_h7)

question: When talking about anticholinergic toxicity, what does the classic phrase 'dry as a bone' mean?

options.A: Extreme brittleness of the bones
options.B: Lack of calcium in the bloodstream
options.C: Loss of sweating and body secretions
options.D: Severe dehydration from diarrhea

explanation: Spot on! It means sweat, saliva, and mucus production completely shut down, leaving the skin and mouth very dry. [learn more](GNS223_U5_T6#GNS223_U5_T6_h5)

question: What administrative penalty can the Nursing and Midwifery Council impose for drug law violations?

options.A: A temporary transfer to a different medical department
options.B: Requiring the nurse to attend a basic computer class
options.C: Suspension or revocation of the nursing practicing license
options.D: Mandatory promotion to a hospital management position

question: Why does lactic acid build up in the body during shock?

options.B: The liver stops filtering waste products from the blood
